land.text: the Roman provinces of Gaul, the Germanies and Raetia, with Britannia, Narbonensis and Hispania following by 261: Postumus 'assumed power in Gaul, Germania, Britannia, and Hispania' (Postumus page)

predecessors.note: A breakaway of the Roman Empire under Gallienus; the roman-empire dossier carries the matching 260 loss.

land.text: Gaul and Britain, reconquered by Aurelian after the Battle of Chalons in 274

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps a Gallic Empire shape to 282; the empire ended in 274 and the 275-282 years are the Roman Empire's.

capitals.name: Colonia Agrippina (Cologne)
capitals.note: Infobox gives 260-271; the dossier's capital years follow the capital_move event of 271, so Cologne is the seat to 270. The page says Postumus 'is thought to have established his capital there or at Augusta Treverorum'.

capitals.name: Augusta Treverorum (Trier)
capitals.note: Infobox 271-274; 'Tetricus established the imperial court at Trier'.

rulers.name: Postumus
rulers.note: Killed by his own troops after retaking Mogontiacum from Laelianus in 269.

rulers.name: Laelianus
rulers.title: usurper
rulers.note: Proclaimed at Mogontiacum in early 269 (Postumus page: 'Within a few months, Postumus was able to capture Mogontiacum and kill Laelianus').

rulers.name: Marius (Marcus Aurelius Marius)
rulers.note: Installed on Postumus's death; the page gives him a few months (some ancient sources two days).

rulers.name: Victorinus
rulers.note: Page body 268/69-271; the infobox gives 269-270. Assassinated in 271.

rulers.name: Domitianus (Domitian II)
rulers.title: usurper
rulers.note: Listed with a question mark on the page, no detail.

rulers.name: Tetricus I
rulers.note: Page body 271-274; the infobox gives 270-274. Tetricus II was caesar from 273.

correction.text: Gaul, Germania Superior and Inferior and Raetia, 'immediately recognized' on Postumus's proclamation (Gallia Narbonensis 'may have been the exception at first'); Cologne is the seat

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Gallic Empire begins in 261, but Postumus was proclaimed in 260 ('around the year 260'; 259 is sometimes favoured, mid-to-late 260 the consensus). At the start the page lists Gaul, Germania Superior and Inferior and Raetia as immediately recognized and has Britannia, Narbonensis and Hispania following 'by 261'.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape plus Hispania, which acknowledged Postumus by 261; the shape holds for 261-268

keyframe_review.note: 261-268: Cliopatria's 261 shape (712,514 km2; France, Belgium and Britain south of c. 55.2 N, bbox 42.4-55.4 N) has no Iberia, but 'By 261, Britannia, Narbonensis and Hispania also acknowledged him as emperor' and the page says he 'assumed power in Gaul, Germania, Britannia, and Hispania'. Hispania is added for 261-268 and leaves in 269 (the next keyframe). The Gallic Empire page gives no area in its infobox, so there is nothing to compare the 0.71 M km2 with.

correction.text: Gaul, the Germanies and Britain without Hispania, after the Spanish provinces deserted the empire in 269

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the single year 269: the Spanish provinces leave. The Postumus page says the empire 'lost Hispania in the meantime' after Marius was made emperor in 269; the Claudius page has 'the Spanish provinces had deserted the Gallic Empire and declared their loyalty to Claudius'. The shape is Cliopatria's 261 shape without Hispania.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without Provence (the Rhone valley of Gaul Claudius regained), for 270-274 only; Gaul, the Germanies and Britain under Victorinus and Tetricus

keyframe_review.note: 270-274: Cliopatria's 270 shape is identical to the 261 one (712,514 km2) and runs to 282, eight years past the empire's end in 274 (Battle of Chalons); 275-282 belong to roman-empire. The Claudius page says he 'regained control of Hispania and the Rhone river valley of Gaul' (his reign 268-270), and the Gallic Empire page that Claudius recovered Narbonensis and parts of Aquitania, which Tetricus 'later retook' in part (western Narbonensis and Aquitania), without dates. The eastern part of Narbonensis (Provence, the Rhone valley) is therefore removed for 270-274 and the western Narbonensis and Aquitaine stay in; the extent is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Gaul, Germania Superior and Inferior and Raetia, 'immediately recognized' on Postumus's proclamation (Gallia Narbonensis 'may have been the exception at first'); Cologne is the seat

ledger.note: 260: Postumus is proclaimed emperor by the army of Gaul and founds the Gallic Empire at Cologne. 'The Roman army in Gaul threw off its allegiance to emperor Gallienus around the year 260'; 'the troops accordingly proclaimed Postumus emperor and besieged Colonia, trapping Saloninus and Silvanus'. The Gallic Empire page: 'established by Postumus in 260' and 'In 260 Postumus besieged Colonia Agrippina and put Saloninus and Silvanus to death'.
261: Britain, Narbonensis and Spain join Postumus. 'By 261, Britannia, Narbonensis and Hispania also acknowledged him as emperor.'

region.text: Raetia, among the regions that recognized Postumus at the start

ledger.note: 261: Raetia is back with Rome. The Postumus page lists Raetia among the regions that recognized him 'immediately' but says nothing of its return; the year follows Cliopatria, whose shapes from 261 do not reach Raetia (page silent).

region.text: the Spanish provinces, which 'deserted the Gallic Empire and declared their loyalty to Claudius'

ledger.note: 269: Spain leaves the Gallic Empire. After Marius is made emperor the page says the Gallic Empire 'lost Hispania in the meantime'; the Claudius Gothicus page: 'He won several victories and soon regained control of Hispania and the Rhone river valley of Gaul' (his reign 268-270). The year is the page's context (Laelianus and Marius, 269), not a dated sentence.

region.text: the Rhone river valley of Gaul, 'southern Gaul' where 'Placidianus had captured Grenoble'

ledger.note: 270: Claudius takes back the Rhone valley. The page says he 'regained control of Hispania and the Rhone river valley of Gaul' without a year inside his reign (268-270); 270 is the researcher's bridge. The Gallic Empire page adds that Claudius 'recovered Narbonensis and parts of Aquitania' and Tetricus 'later retook western Narbonensis and Aquitania', undated; the dossier treats western Narbonensis and Aquitaine as Gallic throughout.
271: the court moves from Cologne to Trier under Tetricus I. Infobox 'Colonia Agrippina (Cologne), 260-271; Augusta Treverorum (Trier), 271-274'; 'Tetricus established the imperial court at Trier'.

274: Aurelian defeats Tetricus at Chalons and ends the Gallic Empire. 'He moved into Gaul and defeated Tetricus at the Battle of Châlons in 274.' The page gives no month. Cliopatria keeps the shape to 282; the empire ended in 274 and the land is the Roman Empire's.

wars.name: Postumus's Rhine campaigns against the Franks and Alamanni
wars.outcome: Postumus held the Rhine limes; the page has him repel mixed groups of Franks and Alamanni in 261 and dates his victories over Franks and Alemanni to 262 and 263 (Postumus page); no border moved.
wars.note: The Gallic Empire page: 'In 261, he repelled mixed groups of Franks and Alamanni to hold the Rhine limes secure' and 'there were no further Germanic raids for ten years'.

wars.name: Gallienus's campaigns against Postumus
wars.outcome: Both campaigns failed and Gallienus never challenged Postumus again; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The Gallic Empire page dates Gallienus's fended-off incursion to 263; the Postumus page dates the campaign to 265 (first attempt failed through the carelessness of the cavalry commander Aureolus; Gallienus himself wounded besieging a Gallic city, possibly Trier). Aureolus turned on Gallienus in 267-268 and declared for Postumus at Milan in 268 without support. Span 263-265 spans both pages.

wars.name: Claudius II's recovery of Spain and the Rhone valley

zones.text: the Rhone river valley of Gaul

wars.outcome: Claudius regained Hispania and the Rhone valley from the Gallic Empire; Victorinus kept Gaul north of it and Britain.
wars.note: Years are the Claudius page's reign (268-270) and the 269 events of the Postumus page; neither dates the recovery.

wars.name: Aurelian's reconquest of the Gallic Empire

zones.text: Gaul, where Tetricus was defeated at Châlons

wars.outcome: Aurelian, having defeated the Palmyrene Empire, 'moved into Gaul and defeated Tetricus at the Battle of Châlons in 274'; the Gallic Empire ended and Gaul and Britain returned to Rome.

certainty.note: No survey or treaty lines; the Rhine limes is the one steady frontier, the Spanish and Narbonensis edges are approximate and the page does not date them.

notes: Cliopatria's two Gallic Empire shapes (261-269, 270-282) are identical (712,514 km2) and end eight years after the empire (274); verdicts in keyframe_review. Cliopatria never reaches Spain (bbox south edge 42.4 N), although both pages have Hispania in the empire in 261; the roman-empire dossier's 260 loss (Gaul and Britain, 'Hispania only briefly') does not carry Spain, so the counterpart loss for the Spanish gain of 261 and the 269 return is missing there, and the Roman Empire shape keeps Spain throughout (an overlap for the rendering agents to resolve). The Gallic Empire page gives no infobox area, so no area comparison was possible. Disagreements: Gallienus's campaign 263 (Gallic Empire page) or 265 (Postumus page); Victorinus 268/69-271 (body) or 269-270 (infobox); Tetricus 271-274 (body) or 270-274 (infobox); Postumus's capital Cologne or Trier. The page is silent on Raetia's return and on the dates of Claudius's and Tetricus's moves in Narbonensis and Aquitaine; those events are confidence 1 or left to the note. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Raetia. Page budget (1-2) exceeded by one page (Claudius Gothicus) to date the Spanish and Rhone recovery.
